one_sentence_story: Benjamin Libet stunned the world in 1983 when motor-cortex voltage ramped up 350 milliseconds before volunteers felt an urge to flick their wrist — until modern neuroscience revealed that ramp was random neural wave-surfing on trivial twitches, while conscious 'free won't' and real deliberate choices work completely differently.
so_what_for_you: Never confuse a random motor impulse with destiny: even on split-second urges you retain a 'free won't' brake window, and meaningful life decisions rely on deliberate prefrontal weighing, not arbitrary wrist-twitch noise.
